MapSandboxHistoryArchiveProtocol

PRESERVATION

The domain is disposable.

Longevity comes from recoverability, independent custody, repeated checking, and migration—not confidence in one medium or company.

Model

QEVA = protocol + open archive + independent mirrors
     + snapshots + institution + right to fork

Rules

  1. Keep original released bytes.
  2. Use publicly documented, character-oriented encodings.
  3. Keep schemas and a human-readable core description beside the data.
  4. Pin dependencies to exact revisions.
  5. Emit more than one fixity digest family when practical.
  6. Do not confuse fixity hashes with authorship or semantic identity.
  7. Place copies under genuinely independent administration.
  8. Read and verify copies periodically; a forgotten dark copy is not enough.
  9. Record every format migration and preserve the source bytes.
  10. Keep the QEVA-native logical archive usable without any proprietary service.
  11. Keep third-party rights and source provenance attached; restricted source content must never become necessary to reconstruct QEVA-native records.

Current release files

SHA-256 repo manifest · SHA-512 repo manifest · recovery bootstrap.

The current logical archive uses JSON/JSONL plus a TSV catalog. This follows a conservative preservation preference for transparent, publicly documented, character-based formats. The archive may later offer BagIt-compatible transfer packages; BagIt is standardized as RFC 8493.

Threat model

FailureDesign response
Domain or host disappearsRelative links, plain files, independent mirrors.
Organization collapsesOpen copying, complete releases, forkable stewardship.
Silent bit rotIndependent manifests plus periodic verification.
One mirror is maliciousCompare independently held copies; no single fixity authority is sacred.
Hash ages badlyAdd new manifest algorithms without deleting old ones.
Format becomes obscureKeep simple text, schema, CORE.txt, and READ-ME-FIRST.txt together.
Meaning driftsImmutable revisions and exact revision-pinned dependencies.
Editor rewrites historyCorrections supersede; released revisions remain inspectable.
External source disappearsPreserve identifiers, provenance, permitted metadata, and reusable snapshots where rights allow.
Rights are misreadTrack source/item licenses separately from QEVA's own CC0 material.

References for today's custodians

JSON: RFC 8259. UTF-8: RFC 3629. BagIt packaging: RFC 8493. These identifiers are duplicated here as names, not treated as permanent web dependencies.
